title: At the table
subtitle: Serving and pairing Viognier
objectives: Know how long to keep it

steps.title: Rich and aromatic dishes
steps.body: Viognier's body and perfume suit rich dishes: roast chicken with apricots, pork, lobster, crab, creamy sauces, and mildly spiced Asian or Moroccan food. Apricot and ginger in dishes echo it. Avoid very acidic or delicate dishes, which make it seem heavy.

steps.title: Service and age
steps.body: Serve at 10 to 13 degrees, not too cold, or its aromas close. Most Viognier is best within three years, when the perfume is fresh. With age, it loses aroma quickly. Château-Grillet and top Condrieu can age a little longer.

steps.prompt: Why is most Viognier best drunk young?
steps.explanation: Its fresh aromas are its charm, and they fade.

steps.body: Try Viognier with a Moroccan chicken tagine with apricots. The fruit and spice match the wine's perfume.

steps.prompt: Viognier generally ages as long as Riesling.
steps.explanation: Not true. Low acidity means most Viognier fades within a few years.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Viognier suits rich, aromatic dishes and apricots
Most is best within three years
